messages:
alex: heads up — support is getting a steady trickle of 502s from hosted API in us-central since ~09:10 UTC. several customers reporting timeouts and failed requests.
sara: saw the pager, joining. any correlation with deploys?
mike: no deploys in last 4 hours. metrics show a spike in upstream 502 responses at the edge/gateway layer starting 09:08. p90 latency for gateway jumped 4x.
linh: digging into gateway logs now — seeing a lot of `connection reset by peer` to inference-backend pods. also some 504s when requests exceed ~10s.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-1798765433, severity P1. War room channel opened.
jordan: @linh can you paste a sample log line with request_id so we can trace?
linh: here are a couple (sanitized):
```
[09:12:03] request_id=r_01G7XJ conn=upstream1 status=502 err="connection reset by peer" path=/v1/generate
[09:12:07] request_id=r_01G8A2 conn=upstream3 status=502 err="read timeout" path=/v1/embeddings
```
alex: support-bot, any common customer pattern? big batches, long sequences, any auth errors?
support-bot: Customer reports: two clients sending large-batch embedding requests (~500 sequences each) starting 09:06, affected 3 tenants. No auth failures logged.
mike: that matches — backend queues show a short-lived surge in large payloads at 09:05-09:14. KV cache hit rate dropped during the surge. suspect memory/kv-cache stall causing worker restarts.
sara: can we failover traffic to eu-west as a short-term mitigation for impacted customers? need to check routing policy and region affinity.
jordan: we can reroute specific tenant keys to eu-west by policy if they allow cross-region. pinging account owner for permission.
linh: meanwhile I'll scale up backend replicas and bump worker timeouts from 10s to 20s for the gateway -> runtime path. applying now.
ops-bot: scaling runtime pool to +4 replicas in us-central (requested by linh).
mike: rolling scale applied. we'll monitor 1m/5m error rates.
linh: quick patch applied: gateway upstream timeout set to 20s. watch logs for restart churn.
alex: ops, add temporary circuit breaker on very large embedding batch size >300 to return 429 with guidance, instead of forwarding to runtime. helps protect the pool.
sara: agree. do it for 30m window and notify customers.
jordan: customer owners for impacted tenants confirmed they accept eu-west failover for now. rerouting set.
linh: post-change logs: still occasional 502 but volume down 90%. no worker OOMs visible. looks like scale + timeout helped.
mike: metrics: request success back to baseline at 09:28. also decreased p95 from 1.8s -> 700ms in gateway.
support-bot: Notifying affected customers of mitigation and asking for any remaining errors.
alex: good containment. now quick postmortem notes in-thread so we can action: root cause hypothesis = sudden large-batch embedding traffic caused kv-cache thrash and upstream runtime connection resets; gateway timeouts were too short and circuit-breakers missing for heavy tail.
sara: action items: 1) implement batch-size limit + graceful 429 for large requests (owner: alex, ETA 3 days) 2) add autoscale policy keyed on queue depth and kv-cache stall signals (owner: mike, ETA 5 days) 3) increase default gateway upstream timeout to 20s with rollout plan (owner: linh, ETA 1 day) 4) add synthetic load test covering large-batch embeddings and observability (owner: jordan, ETA 7 days).
jordan: + add a log field `kv_cache_latency_ms` and alert when >500ms for >1m. owner: mike.
linh: also recommend improving runtime healthcheck to detect hung workers (owner: linh, ETA 3 days).
ops-bot: Recording action items to INC-1798765433 and creating follow-up tickets.
sara: schedule a 30-min postmortem sync tomorrow 10:00 UTC — invite eng-runtime, eng-platform, support, and account owners.
mike: quick note for support: if customer sees 502, ask for request_id header and exact timestamp window; saves time.
alex: thanks everyone. final state: traffic stabilized, mitigation applied (scale + timeout + temp circuit-break), customers rerouted where approved. we’ll close war room once follow-ups are assigned and the 24h stability window passes. :thumbsup:
support-bot: Customers acknowledged. No new errors reported in the last 10m.
ops-bot: Last update at 09:59 UTC. Incident remains open for postmortem actions.
